pages.title: Fixed-generator positive factorizations in Wajnryb's Artin A5 quotient
pages.description: Classifies fixed-generator positive words in Wajnryb’s Artin A5 quotient: lengths 20, 30, 40, with four strict Hurwitz classes and three up to conjugation.
pages.author: Alec Kriebel
pages.abstract: We classify the positive words in the five standard generators of B₆/⟨⟨ch⁻¹⟩⟩ representing c², where c=(a₁a₂a₃a₄)⁵ and h=a₅a₄a₃a₂a₁²a₂a₃a₄a₅. Their lengths are 20, 30, 40, with respectively one, one, and two strict Hurwitz classes. Simultaneous conjugation identifies the two length-40 classes, giving the three representatives proposed in Wajnryb's question. The proof combines classical geometric and braid results with pure-braid linking constraints and an exhaustive, exact 810-word certificate for the length-20 case. The length spectrum and the twice-per-pair crossing theorem used at length 30 have prior sources; a reproducible six-strand certificate for the latter is supplied as additional evidence.

pages.title: A characteristic-two counterexample to dévissage for local deformation functors
pages.description: For a standard characteristic-two local action, no prorepresentable recipient makes restriction–induction formally smooth, in any tangent dimension.
pages.author: Alec Kriebel
pages.abstract: We give a negative answer to the unrestricted fibre-product question for local deformation functors posed by Byszewski. For the weakly ramified action of the additive group of F₄ given by t↦t/(1+at), and its subgroup F₂, restriction–induction cannot be formally smooth over any prorepresentable recipient, regardless of its tangent dimension. The proof combines the known involution deformation pathology with an exact calculation showing that restriction has injective tangent map. The variant assuming prorepresentability of the subgroup and quotient deformation functors is untouched. The involution pathology and additive action are established prior ingredients; the contribution is their use to obstruct the proposed factorization.

pages.title: A fixed birational map without a prime-field cycle-distribution limit
pages.description: A fixed birational map has no limiting point-weighted period distribution on positive-upper-density prime selections, using classical arithmetic inputs.
pages.author: Alec Kriebel
pages.abstract: For the fixed birational map L(u,v)=(u,(u^2+1)v), reduction at every prime p≡3(mod 4) permutes all of F_p^2. Its point-weighted distribution of periods divided by p has no limit. At every fixed 1/2≤ x<1, the distribution function is 1-φ(p-1)/(p-1)+o(1), with limsup 1 and liminf at most 23/24. Moreover, neither these distribution-function values nor the period measures converge on any further prime subset of positive upper relative density. The latter statement uses the classical continuous empirical law for φ(p-1)/(p-1). A supplementary proposition treats all odd primes on the invariant regular domain, and under uniform-point deletion or arbitrary exceptional-period completion. These conventions cannot restore convergence on any positive-upper-density prime selection. The contribution is a precisely delimited application to the broad existence assertion in the 2004 Oberwolfach problem on finite-field maps. The triangular family, primitive-value estimates, totient mean and scalar distribution law are established ingredients; no new arithmetic theorem or historical firstness is claimed.

blocks.text: Set L(u,v)=(u,(u²+1)v), with rational inverse L⁻¹(u,v)=(u,v/(u²+1)). It is a fixed infinite-order birational map over Q with invariant u and genus-zero generic invariant fibers. Put S={p prime : p≡3 (mod 4)}. For every p in S the reduction permutes all of F_p². If T_p(z) is a point’s least positive period, define μ_p=(1/p²)Σ_{z∈F_p²}δ_{T_p(z)/p} and D_p(x)=μ_p([0,x]). These are uniform point weights and normalization by p.

pages.title: A Lipschitz-nonincreasing deformation of small unitary-valued maps
pages.description: An explicit deformation of small unitary-valued sphere maps preserves a half-Lipschitz bound, with a quantitative estimate for two intrinsic length metrics.
pages.author: Alec Kriebel
pages.abstract: For the unit-round sphere and either the unnormalized Hilbert–Schmidt or operator-norm length metric on U(N), we give an explicit strong deformation retraction of the maps with Lipschitz constant at most 1/2 onto the constant maps. At time t ∈ [0,1], the Lipschitz constant is at most (1 − t²)/(1 + t²) times its original value. The formula depends continuously on the entire map and stays in the original U(N). In particular, it answers the literal question [?24](i) in Gromov's 2017 scalar-curvature problem list, with the stronger requirement that the Lipschitz bound be preserved throughout. pages.title: A regular zero-area singularity with a nonzero weak Bianchi defect
pages.description: A classical negative-mass geometry has regular zero-area singularities on static slices but a nonzero weak Bianchi boundary functional under retained-sphere vector tests.
pages.author: Alec Kriebel
pages.abstract: We apply a negative-mass member of the known Dadhich–Kar–Mukherjee–Visser metric family to the regular-zero-area-singularity conjecture in Burtscher's Oberwolfach report. Its natural static slices have harmonically regular zero-area singularities of mass −2a, but the homogeneous weak second Bianchi identity fails under the boundary-reaching vector-test convention of Burtscher–Kiessling–Tahvildar-Zadeh. We prove absolute convergence of the full scalar contraction for every such compactly supported smooth test and compute its exact boundary functional; a normalized radial test gives −8π. The metric and its Einstein tensor are classical, and the flux method is already present in the cited weak-identity work. The contribution is this explicit counterexample application and its convergence check. The example violates the null energy condition. The conclusion concerns the geometric implication in the cited static-foliation framework, with no specified matter model; it asserts neither regularity on every arbitrary tilted slice nor an identity for tests smooth after collapsing the boundary sphere to a point.
